This is an fMRI study of alcohol pictures versus neutral and scrambled pictures in adult men (I1, I2 met). Whole-brain MNI coordinates are reported (I4 met). The reported contrasts are not a within-group cue versus neutral contrast. Table 2 is alcoholics versus controls for the alcohol-versus-control contrast. Tables 3 and 4 are before versus after amisulpride, also for the alcohol-versus-control contrast. No within-group cue > neutral or baseline result is reported, so I3 was not demonstrated.

Adult smokers viewed smoking and control pictures, and the smoking > control contrast was reported (I1, I2, I3 met). The analysis was restricted to a mask of pre-selected regions at uncorrected P ≤ 0.005. It is therefore not whole-brain, and whole-brain coordinates were not shown (I4 not met, E1 met). Tables 2 and 3 were not supplied. The study cites the parent trial but reports its own genotype analysis, so E2 is not met.

Adult heroin-dependent and control participants viewed heroin-cue and neutral videos (I1, I2 met). Table I lists whole-brain Talairach coordinates (I4 met). Those coordinates are for the cue-type by group interaction, a between-group effect. No within-group cue vs neutral whole-brain contrast is reported, so I3 is not_met.

Adults viewed erotic vs neutral film excerpts (I1, I2 met). Within-group erotic > neutral contrasts were run (I3 met), but they are shown only as figures. The only coordinates, in Table 1, are for between-group comparisons (male vs female, male vs MTF) at a priori ROIs with uncorrected thresholds. No whole-brain peak coordinates for cue vs neutral are reported (I4 not met). Coordinates are ROI-only (E1 met).

Adult smokers (18-50) viewed smoking and neutral images in fMRI (I1, I2 met). The reported contrasts compare the control and exercise conditions. The text states there was no significant difference between smoking and neutral images, so no within-group cue versus neutral or baseline contrast is shown (I3 not demonstrated, so not_met). Table 1 coordinates are for control and exercise conditions and were not supplied.

Adult women viewed food photographs, with fattening food > object contrasts (I1, I2, I3 met). All analyses used predefined regions of interest (13 anatomical masks). The authors say they limited the investigation to regions of interest and that whole-brain analyses are still needed. The tables report only ROI cluster coordinates, so no whole-brain coordinates exist (I4 not met, E1 met).

Adult female smokers viewed smoking vs neutral images (I1, I2 met). Whole-brain Talairach results are cited (Table S1, not supplied), so I4 is met. However, the only whole-brain cue contrast reported is a between-group comparison (slip > abstinent) of smoking>neutral. No within-group cue vs neutral contrast is reported, so I3 was not demonstrated. The ICA connectivity maps are not cue contrasts.

Adult men viewed erotic films. The reported within-group contrasts are only the disgust-inducing sexual stimuli versus rest (F–F in homosexual men, M–M in heterosexual men), and the paper frames them as disgust processing. No reward-cue (sexually arousing) versus neutral or baseline contrast is reported, so I3 is not met. Coordinates are reported, but they are for aversive stimuli, not reward cue reactivity.

Adult women smokers viewed smoking and neutral images (I1, I2 met). The only whole-brain results are correlations between smoking>neutral reactivity and Stroop attentional bias. No within-group smoking vs neutral contrast is reported (I3 not met). Talairach coordinates are given for the correlation clusters. About 21 of 28 subjects overlap with a prior study, but this is not a pure reanalysis.
Participants were adolescents aged 13 to 17, so I1 is not met. The study otherwise fits: smoking-cue vs neutral-cue fMRI with whole-brain MNI coordinates in Table 2. Excluded on I1 only.

Adult alcohol-dependent participants viewed alcohol vs neutral beverage pictures (I1, I2, I3 met). Results come from anatomical and functional ROIs. The functional analysis was restricted to a striatum mask. No whole-brain coordinates are reported, so E1 is met and I4 is not met.

Adult cocaine users watched cocaine and food videos in fMRI, and the whole-brain cocaine-versus-food and group contrasts are in Talairach space (I1–I3 met). The only coordinate table (Table 2) holds resting-state connectivity results. The text gives no peak coordinates for the cocaine-cue activations and cites no table for them; it describes them only by region and in figures. Whole-brain stereotaxic peak coordinates for cue reactivity were therefore not demonstrated (I4 not met).

Adult men viewed erotic vs neutral pictures (I1, I2, I3 met). The coordinate table (Table 1) comes from ROI analyses with small-volume correction (E1 met). The only whole-brain peak in the text is one right inferior occipital gyrus peak for mSEX-aversive, which is not a cue-vs-neutral contrast. No whole-brain cue-vs-neutral coordinates are reported (I4 not met).

Adult males viewed heroin vs neutral images, and the heroin>neutral contrast was run (I1–I3 met). The task results are only described by region names and shown in Fig. 6. The only coordinates are the resting-state degree foci in Table 2 and two correlation ROIs (meFG, ACC). No whole-brain peak coordinates for the cue>neutral contrast are reported, so I4 is not demonstrated.

Adult cocaine-cue fMRI study (I1, I2 met). Table 2 reports MNI coordinates, including exploratory whole-brain peaks. However, the only Cocaine>Neutral results reported are between-group (patients > controls) and modafinil-vs-placebo interaction contrasts. No within-group cue-versus-neutral contrast is reported, so I3 is not met.

Adult alcohol-dependent patients and controls viewed alcohol vs neutral pictures during fMRI (I1, I2 met). Peak MNI coordinates are reported, with whole-brain results in eTables (I4 met). However, every reported cue>neutral result is a between-group comparison (REL vs CON, ABS vs REL, ABS vs CON). No within-group cue vs neutral contrast is reported, so I3 was not demonstrated.

Adult smokers and nonsmokers viewed or touched smoking objects and control objects (I1, I2 met). The reported results are main effects and interactions: object category across both groups (control > smoking), group × category, and a three-way interaction. No within-group smoking vs control contrast is reported, so I3 was not demonstrated. Coordinate tables were not supplied. The text says the maps were whole-brain corrected.

Participants were adults aged 21–60. Alcohol beverage pictures were embedded as distractors in an oddball task. Whole-brain peak coordinates are given only for the Group-by-Distractor interaction and for the craving correlation. The within-group AD vs NAD contrast in healthy controls was described only qualitatively at an uncorrected threshold, with no coordinates. So no within-group cue vs neutral contrast with whole-brain coordinates was demonstrated (I3 and I4 not met).

Marijuana cue versus non-marijuana cue fMRI in adults, so I1-I3 are met. The reported coordinates come only from an analysis masked to a priori ROIs (amygdala, ventral striatum, OFC, insula, hippocampus). Unmasked whole-brain data are only on a website, not reported as peak coordinates. E1 is met and I4 is not met.

Adult women (mean age about 20) viewed chocolate vs neutral pictures (I1, I2 met). Whole-brain Talairach coordinates are reported (I4 met). However, the only coordinate tables are group × picture type and 3-way interaction F-maps. No within-group chocolate > neutral contrast with coordinates is reported, so I3 is not demonstrated.

Adults 18-65 viewed cocaine vs neutral pictures in fMRI (I1, I2 met). Table 2 gives whole-brain MNI peaks (I4 met). Only the between-group contrast (UDS+ > UDS−) of cocaine-minus-neutral activation is reported. No within-group cue vs neutral contrast is reported, so I3 is not met.

Adult women viewed erotic pictures in fMRI (I1, I2 met). Table 2 gives whole-brain Talairach coordinates (I4 met). The only cue-versus-neutral contrast pools erotic, romantic, mutilation and sad pictures against neutral, so it is a general emotional-versus-neutral contrast. It is not a reward-cue-versus-neutral contrast, and no erotic > neutral result is reported. Table 3 gives the group × category interaction, which is a between-group effect and not a cue-versus-neutral contrast. I3 is not met.

Participants were 18–21-year-old college students who viewed alcohol pictures, so I1 and I2 are met. The whole-brain analysis was a between-group ANOVA on alcohol vs non-alcohol images. Table 3 gives Talairach coordinates only for the group-difference F clusters. The within-group cue vs neutral or baseline results were post-hoc tests on extracted cluster averages, with no whole-brain coordinates. So I3 and I4 were not demonstrated.

Adult heroin patients saw heroin-related and neutral pictures (I1, I2 met). Drug cues > neutral was tested within group (I3 met). The only coordinates are in Tables 3 and 4, and they come from analyses restricted to an explicit OFC mask. The whole-brain effects (occipital, medial frontal, inferior frontal) are described in the text with no peak coordinates. The abstract calls the analyses region of interest. So whole-brain coordinates are not reported (I4 not met, E1 met).

Adults viewed cigarette video cues and received alcohol taste cues (I1, I2 met). The analysis is precuneus ROI only. The coordinates given are mean leave-one-out ROI peaks, not whole-brain results. No whole-brain cue > control peak table is reported (I3 and I4 not_met, E1 met).

Adults viewed alcohol cue videos against a mosaic control, in fMRI with Talairach coordinates (I1, I2 and I4 met). Table 2 lists only between-group contrasts (PAD vs healthy controls). It gives no within-group cue vs neutral peaks, so I3 was not demonstrated. The study reports whole-brain results, so E1 is not met.

Adults viewed sexual pictures, and sex > neutral contrasts were computed, so I1 to I3 are met. All analyses were ROI analyses with small-volume correction, and the coordinate tables list peaks within ROIs only. No whole-brain coordinates are reported, so E1 is met and I4 is not met. The sample overlaps with a prior first-assessment study, but this is not a pure reanalysis.

Adult male heroin patients and controls viewed heroin and neutral pictures (I1 and I2 met). Whole-brain peak coordinates are reported in Tables 2 and 3 (I4 met). However, every reported fMRI result is a between-group comparison of the heroin>neutral contrast: patients vs controls, relapsers vs controls, and relapsers vs non-relapsers. No within-group cue vs neutral contrast is reported, so I3 is not demonstrated.

Participants were adolescents aged 16.0–18.9 years, mostly under 18 (I1 not met). Alcohol vs neutral beverage cues are used, but the reported coordinates are for between-group differences (HD vs CON) in the baseline, not within-group cue>neutral contrasts (I3, I4 not demonstrated).

Smoking vs neutral video cues were shown during fMRI (I2 met), and the smoking > neutral contrast was modeled (I3 met). The sample includes adolescents aged 13–18 (mean 17.5, some under 18) analysed together with adults, so I1 is not met. The whole-brain main-effect table is only in an unsupplied supplementary table, and the reported analyses are ROI-based. Peak coordinates were not demonstrated for a whole-brain cue contrast.

Adult obese participants viewed food and non-food images (I1 and I2 met). The reported analyses are between-group comparisons (prediabetic vs nondiabetic) and regressions on MetS criteria. No within-group food versus non-food contrast is reported (I3 not met). Results come from small-volume correction in spherical ROIs, with no whole-brain peak coordinates in the text (E1 met, I4 not met).

Adults aged 18–30 viewed cannabis images versus neutral images and baseline. However, analyses were restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume FWE correction, and only ROI peaks are reported. No whole-brain coordinates were reported, so I4 is not met and E1 is met.

Participants were adolescents aged 14-19 (mean about 16.5), so most were under 18 and I1 is not met. Other criteria are met: food cue task, appetizing/plain > baseline contrast, whole-brain MNI coordinates.

Adult alcohol-dependent patients viewed alcohol vs non-alcoholic beverage pictures (I1, I2 met). Group-level analyses were only AD vs HC and treatment x time interactions; no within-group cue vs neutral contrast was reported (I3 not demonstrated). Peak coordinates are small-volume-corrected ROI results; whole-brain results are only uncorrected group comparisons in unsupplied supplementary tables (I4 not demonstrated).

The sample is 35 adolescents aged 14–19 years (mean 17.2). This includes minors, so I1 is not met. The food image task, with food > non-food contrasts and whole-brain results, would otherwise qualify (I2, I3 and I4 met). The whole-brain table is Supplemental Table 1, which was not supplied.

Adult male cannabis users and controls viewed cannabis and neutral pictures in fMRI (I1, I2 met). Whole-brain peak coordinates in MNI space are in Table 4 (I4 met). However, the reported contrasts are between-group differences in cue reactivity (users > controls). The text shows no within-group cannabis > neutral contrast with coordinates, so I3 was not demonstrated.

Adults viewed alcohol and juice beverage images against a mosaic baseline, but the reported whole-brain results are group main effects and stimulus-by-group interaction F-tests (Table 2), not a within-group cue vs neutral/baseline contrast. Post hoc comparisons are between-group ROI extractions. No within-group cue > baseline contrast was reported, so I3 was not demonstrated.
